claim: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is caused by mutations of the Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator (CFTR) anion channel.
source: The devastating inherited disease cystic fibrosis (CF) is caused by mutations of the Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator (CFTR) anion channel.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the genetic basis of cystic fibrosis.

claim: Ivacaftor (Vx-770) is a CFTR potentiator drug approved for the treatment of CF patients.
source: The recent approval of the CFTR potentiator drug ivacaftor (Vx-770) for the treatment of CF patients has marked the advent of causative CF therapy.
evidence: This refers to FDA approval and clinical use, which is established knowledge.

claim: The aqueous solubility of Vx-770 is approximately 60 nanomolar at 25°C and pH 7.1.
source: Considering that Vx-770 was concentrated 20-fold during the extraction procedure, we conclude that the true aqueous solubility of Vx-770 at 25°C is only ~60 nM (Saq(25°C, pH = 7.1)=62 ± 2 nM, n = 4)
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements using spectrophotometry and extraction methods described in the manuscript.

claim: The aqueous solubility of Vx-770 is approximately 200-fold lower than previously reported.
source: we conclude that the true aqueous solubility of Vx-770 at 25°C is only ~60 nM (Saq(25°C, pH = 7.1)=62 ± 2 nM, n = 4), almost 200-fold lower than generally believed
evidence: This is based on comparison of measured data with previously reported values.

claim: Vx-770 is extremely soluble in anhydrous dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) with solubility approximately 0.77 M.
source: We found Vx-770 extremely soluble in anhydrous dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) (S ~ 0.77 M)
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements shown in Table 1.

claim: Vx-770 is reasonably soluble in 1-octanol with solubility approximately 3.9 mM.
source: reasonably soluble in 1-octanol (S ~ 3.9 mM)
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements shown in Table 1.

claim: Vx-770 is reasonably soluble in ethanol with solubility approximately 3.1 mM.
source: reasonably soluble in 1-octanol (S ~ 3.9 mM) and ethanol (S ~ 3.1 mM)
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements shown in Table 1.

claim: CFTR channel stimulation by Vx-770 is fully reversible in cell-free patches.
source: upon drug removal the current readily declined back to its pre-drug value (time constant τ ~2 min, Figure 2a, red fit line), demonstrating full reversibility of Vx-770 effects.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a and described in the text.

claim: Previous reports of irreversible CFTR channel stimulation by Vx-770 were due to use of supersaturated drug concentrations.
source: in contrast to those earlier studies, the observed effects on channel gating were fully reversible following washout of the drug (Figure 2b, bottom trace; Figure 2c, light gray bars).
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of current results with previous studies and the finding that supersaturated concentrations were used previously.

claim: The K0.5 of Vx-770 for stimulation of WT CFTR is approximately 0.47-0.49 nM.
source: a dose response curve (Figure 3c, red symbols), obtained by assuming [Vx-770]=62 nM in our 1x saturated stock (cf., Table 1), yielded a K0.5 of 0.47 ± 0.12 nM (Figure 3c, red fit line).
evidence: This is supported by dose-response experimental data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The apparent K0.5 of Vx-770 for stimulation of WT CFTR is approximately 600-fold lower than previously reported.
source: Thus, the apparent K0.5 of Vx-770 for stimulation of WT CFTR is ~600 fold lower than previously reported (~300 nM [Van Goor et al., 2014; Langron et al., 2018]).
evidence: This is based on comparison of measured data with previously published values.

claim: Vx-770 stimulates WT CFTR currents approximately 4-fold at saturating concentrations.
source: application of our 1x saturated Vx-770 solution (red bar) to prephosphorylated WT CFTR channels opened by 2 mM ATP (gray bar) caused rapid robust (~4 fold) current stimulation
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Vx-770 stimulates G551D CFTR currents approximately 11-12-fold at saturating concentrations.
source: For both mutants maximal current stimulation was 11–12-fold with a K0.5 of ~1.5 nM (Figure 3f, blue and green symbols and fit lines)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3d and 3f.

claim: Vx-770 stimulates ΔF508 CFTR currents approximately 11-12-fold at saturating concentrations.
source: For both mutants maximal current stimulation was 11–12-fold with a K0.5 of ~1.5 nM (Figure 3f, blue and green symbols and fit lines)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3e and 3f.

claim: The K0.5 of Vx-770 for G551D CFTR is approximately 1.5 nM.
source: For both mutants maximal current stimulation was 11–12-fold with a K0.5 of ~1.5 nM (Figure 3f, blue and green symbols and fit lines)
evidence: This is supported by dose-response experimental data shown in Figure 3f.

claim: The K0.5 of Vx-770 for ΔF508 CFTR is approximately 1.5 nM.
source: For both mutants maximal current stimulation was 11–12-fold with a K0.5 of ~1.5 nM (Figure 3f, blue and green symbols and fit lines)
evidence: This is supported by dose-response experimental data shown in Figure 3f.

claim: The true potency of Vx-770 for G551D CFTR is approximately 200-fold higher than previously reported.
source: Thus, the true potency of Vx-770 for G551D CFTR is ~200 fold higher, and for ΔF508 CFTR 20–300-fold higher, than previously reported (Van Goor et al., 2009; Yu et al., 2012; Van Goor et al., 2014; Langron et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on comparison of measured data with previously published values.

claim: The true potency of Vx-770 for ΔF508 CFTR is 20-300-fold higher than previously reported.
source: Thus, the true potency of Vx-770 for G551D CFTR is ~200 fold higher, and for ΔF508 CFTR 20–300-fold higher, than previously reported (Van Goor et al., 2009; Yu et al., 2012; Van Goor et al., 2014; Langron et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on comparison of measured data with previously published values.

claim: Vx-770 stimulation of CFTR channels shows sigmoidal activation kinetics with marked delay at low concentrations.
source: In contrast, the activation time course upon drug exposure was clearly sigmoidal, suggesting the presence of multiple sequential slow steps in the activation pathway.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: At least three sequential concentration-dependent slow steps are required to fit the activation time course of Vx-770 effects.
source: Indeed, at least three sequential concentration-dependent slow steps were required to obtain an adequate fit (Figure 4a, blue fit lines).
evidence: This is based on kinetic modeling of experimental data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Deactivation kinetics following Vx-770 wash-off can be fitted with a single exponential.
source: The kinetics of current deactivation following Vx-770 wash-off was well fitted assuming a single rate-limiting step (Figure 4a, green single-exponential fit lines and time constants τ).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and fitting shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Vx-770 increases the opening rate of WT CFTR channels.
source: Stimulation of open probability was due to acceleration of channel opening and slowing of channel closure (Figure 2b, top and center trace; Figure 2c, red vs. dark gray bars)
evidence: This is supported by single-channel experimental data shown in Figure 2b and 2c.

claim: Vx-770 decreases the closing rate of WT CFTR channels.
source: Stimulation of open probability was due to acceleration of channel opening and slowing of channel closure (Figure 2b, top and center trace; Figure 2c, red vs. dark gray bars)
evidence: This is supported by single-channel experimental data shown in Figure 2b and 2c.

claim: A kinetic model with two independent drug binding sites provides a good fit to Vx-770 activation/deactivation time courses.
source: Interestingly, although it contains no additional free parameters relative to Scheme 1, Scheme 3 provided a dramatically improved ensemble fit, yielding a single set of rate constants (Figure 5e, left) that can reasonably account for the current activation and deactivation time courses observed in response to addition and removal of Vx-770, over a 100-fold concentration range (Figure 5f, blue fit lines).
evidence: This is supported by kinetic modeling and fitting of experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The octanol/water distribution coefficient of Vx-770 at pH 7.1 is approximately 62,580.
source: To reduce the number of free parameters in the considered models, the equilibrium ratio of membrane-dissolved and aqueous concentrations of Vx-770 (i.e., the ratio kin/kout, Figure 5a–d) was fixed to its measured octanol/water distribution coefficient (Doct/wat(pH=7.1)=62580, logD = 4.8, cf., Table 1)
evidence: This is calculated from measured solubilities in octanol and water shown in Table 1.

claim: The aqueous solubility of Vx-770 at pH 7.4 and 25°C is approximately 50 nM.
source: From three independent measurements we obtained an estimate of Saq(25°C, pH = 7.4) = 50 ± 1 nM (mean ± S.E.M.)
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements described in the methods.

claim: The aqueous solubility of Vx-770 is similar at pH 7.1 and pH 7.4.
source: which is not larger than that obtained for pH = 7.1, the small difference likely reflecting experimental limitations. This finding suggests that the strongest acidic pKa value of the drug is substantially higher than 7.4
evidence: This is based on comparison of measured solubilities at different pH values.

claim: The aqueous solubility of Vx-770 at 37°C and pH 7.1 is approximately 138 nM.
source: Vx-770 aqueous solubility at 37°C was ~2 fold higher compared to that at 25°C, three independent measurements yielding an estimate of Saq(37°C, pH = 7.1) = 138 ± 1 nM (mean ± S.E.M.).
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements described in the methods.

claim: The aqueous solubility of Vx-770 at 37°C is approximately 2-fold higher than at 25°C.
source: Consistent with reports for other hydrophobic drugs (Baena et al., 2004; Garzón and Martínez, 2004; Mota et al., 2009), Vx-770 aqueous solubility at 37°C was ~2 fold higher compared to that at 25°C
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements and comparison with literature on other drugs.

claim: The standard enthalpy of solution for Vx-770 is +51.2 kJ/mol.
source: The standard enthalpy of solution, estimated from the solubilities at 37°C vs. 25°C, is ΔHosol = +51.2 kJ/mol
evidence: This is calculated from measured solubilities at different temperatures.

claim: The standard free energy of solution for Vx-770 at 25°C is +41.1 kJ/mol.
source: and the standard free energy of solution at 25°C is ΔGosol = +41.1 kJ/mol (Materials and methods).
evidence: This is calculated from measured solubility data.

claim: CFTR belongs to the family of ATP Binding Cassette (ABC) proteins.
source: CFTR belongs to the family of ATP Binding Cassette (ABC) proteins (Riordan et al., 1989)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: CFTR forms an anion selective channel that is activated by phosphorylation of its regulatory domain by PKA.
source: and forms an anion selective channel which is activated by phosphorylation of its cytosolic regulatory (R) domain by cyclic AMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA) (Berger et al., 1991; Tabcharani et al., 1991).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In phosphorylated CFTR channels, gating is coupled to conformational changes induced by ATP binding and hydrolysis at two nucleotide binding domains.
source: In phosphorylated CFTR channels opening and closing (gating) of the anion pore is coupled to conformational changes induced by ATP binding and hydrolysis at two cytosolic nucleotide binding domains (NBDs) (Anderson et al., 1991; Li et al., 1996).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The most common CF mutation, deletion of phenylalanine 508 (ΔF508), is present in approximately 90% of CF patients.
source: The most common CF mutation, deletion of phenylalanine 508 (ΔF508), is present in ~90% of patients
evidence: This is established knowledge about CF genetics.

claim: The ΔF508 mutation impairs both channel surface expression and open probability.
source: The most common CF mutation, deletion of phenylalanine 508 (ΔF508), is present in ~90% of patients and impairs both channel surface expression (Cheng et al., 1990) and open probability (Miki et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Vx-770 was approved by the FDA for treatment of patients carrying G551D and other gating mutations.
source: The potentiator Vx-770 (Van Goor et al., 2009), identified by Vertex Pharmaceuticals using high-throughput screening, has proven successful and was approved by the FDA for the treatment of patients carrying G551D and other gating mutations (Ramsey et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about FDA approval supported by citation.

claim: Patients carrying the ΔF508 mutation experienced significant clinical improvement from co-administration of Vx-770 with corrector drugs in phase two clinical trials.
source: Moreover, in a recent phase two clinical trial, patients carrying the most common CF mutation ΔF508 also experienced significant clinical improvement from co-administration of Vx-770 with a combination of corrector drugs (Boyle et al., 2014; Wainwright et al., 2015; Davies et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to clinical trial results.

claim: Previous studies reported that CFTR channel stimulation by Vx-770 in cell-free patches is irreversible.
source: Thus, CFTR channel stimulation by Vx-770 in cell-free patches is reportedly irreversible (Jih and Hwang, 2013; Lin et al., 2016; Yeh et al., 2015; Yeh et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2018)
evidence: This summarizes findings from previous studies supported by citations.

claim: Maximal stimulation of WT CFTR channels by Vx-770 shows large variability in previous reports, ranging from approximately 1.1-fold to 3-fold.
source: maximal stimulation of WT CFTR channels shows large variability (ranging from ~1.1 fold [Cui and McCarty, 2015] to ~3 fold [Wang et al., 2018])
evidence: This summarizes findings from previous studies supported by citations.

claim: In some studies, acute application of Vx-770 caused or accentuated CFTR channel inactivation.
source: and in some studies its acute application caused (Cholon et al., 2014) – or accentuated (Wang et al., 2014) – CFTR channel inactivation.
evidence: This summarizes findings from previous studies supported by citations.

claim: Vx-770 is routinely used at concentrations up to 10 μM in published studies.
source: Vx-770 is routinely used at concentrations up to 10 μM (Cui and McCarty, 2015; Langron et al., 2018; Liu and Dawson, 2014; Van Goor et al., 2009; Van Goor et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2018)
evidence: This summarizes common practice in previous studies supported by citations.

claim: All published in vitro studies have used Vx-770 at supersaturated concentrations ranging from 100 nM to 10 μM.
source: Because in all published in vitro studies Vx-770 was applied at concentrations ranging from 100 nM to 10 μM (Cui and McCarty, 2015; Yeh et al., 2015; Yeh et al., 2017; Langron et al., 2018; Liu and Dawson, 2014; Van Goor et al., 2009; Van Goor et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2018; DeStefano et al., 2018; Jih and Hwang, 2013; Lin et al., 2016; Kopeikin et al., 2014), our present solubility estimate indicates that Vx-770 effects have so far been characterized only at supersaturated concentrations.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of measured solubility with concentrations used in previous studies.

claim: Supersaturated concentrations of Vx-770 may explain previously reported channel inactivation.
source: Such precipitates might have contributed to CFTR channel inactivation observed in some studies (Cholon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the finding of supersaturation and previous observations.

claim: Supersaturated concentrations of Vx-770 may explain previously reported irreversibility of drug effects through formation of intramembrane crystalline precipitates.
source: Moreover, following removal of Vx-770 from the aqueous perfusate, the membrane-dissolved drug pool might be replenished from such intra-membrane crystalline precipitates as long as the crystals last (which will depend on the degree of supersaturation of the applied aqueous test solution, and on exposure time), explaining the reported irreversibility of drug effects (Jih and Hwang, 2013; Lin et al., 2016; Yeh et al., 2015; Yeh et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the finding of supersaturation and previous observations.

claim: Peak plasma concentrations of approximately 4 μM and >10 μM have been measured in patients receiving 150 mg and 450 mg doses of Vx-770, respectively.
source: Vx-770 shows good oral bioavailability, and peak plasma concentrations of ~4 μM, and >10 μM, respectively, have been measured in patients receiving twice daily 150 mg (therapeutic) or 450 mg (supratherapeutic) doses (FDA report by Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated, https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203188Orig1s000OtherRedt.pdf).
evidence: This is based on FDA pharmacokinetic data cited in the manuscript.

claim: Most Vx-770 in plasma is bound to plasma proteins.
source: In the plasma, most of the drug is bound to plasma proteins
evidence: This is established pharmacokinetic knowledge.

claim: Cell membranes are at equilibrium with free dissolved Vx-770, not with protein-bound drug.
source: On the other hand, cell membranes are at equilibrium with free dissolved Vx-770, not with the protein-bound drug.
evidence: This is based on established principles of drug distribution and pharmacokinetics.

claim: The dominant microspecies of Vx-770 in the physiological pH range is the fully protonated uncharged form.
source: This finding suggests that the strongest acidic pKa value of the drug is substantially higher than 7.4, and so the uncharged, fully protonated form remains the dominant microspecies in the entire physiological pH range.
evidence: This is inferred from the pH-independence of solubility measurements.

claim: The distribution of Vx-770 between cytosol and extracellular space is unaffected by the transmembrane pH gradient and membrane potential.
source: Consequently, the distribution of the drug between the cytosol and extracellular space is unaffected by the transmembrane pH gradient and the membrane potential.
evidence: This is inferred from the finding that the drug remains uncharged in the physiological pH range.

claim: The apparent second-order on-rates of Vx-770 obtained from kinetic modeling are several orders of magnitude slower than expected for diffusion-limited binding.
source: Considering that measured diffusion coefficients of small molecules within a lipid bilayer fall in the range of 10−8 to 10−7 cm2/s (Ladha et al., 1996; Macháň and Hof, 2010), the apparent second-order on-rates (kon') of Vx-770 obtained from the fits to Scheme 3 are several orders of magnitude slower than expected for diffusion-limited binding of membrane-dissolved drug molecules to the CFTR protein.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of fitted rate constants with literature values for diffusion coefficients.

claim: Vx-770 may remain associated with the polar surface of the lipid bilayer due to its hydrogen bonding capability.
source: One possible explanation for this slow apparent on-rate could be that the drug remains associated with the polar surface of the bilayer, consistent with the hydrogen bonding capability of its five polar groups (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the chemical structure and kinetic data.

claim: Two drug molecules need to bind to the CFTR channel protein to achieve potentiation.
source: Two common mechanistic conclusions suggested by the Scheme-3 and Scheme-4 fits are that (i) two drug molecules need to bind to the channel protein to achieve potentiation
evidence: This is inferred from kinetic modeling of experimental data.

claim: The slow channel deactivation following drug removal reflects slow dissociation of bound drug from the protein rather than slow washout from the membrane.
source: and that (ii) the slow channel deactivation time course following drug removal reflects the slow dissociation rate of the bound drug from the protein (koff), rather than slow washout of unbound drug molecules from the membrane (kout).
evidence: This is inferred from kinetic modeling of experimental data.

claim: Half-maximal CFTR potentiation is achieved by an approximately 100-fold dilution of a saturated Vx-770 solution.
source: A clinically relevant aspect of our findings is that half-maximal CFTR potentiation is achieved already by an ~100 fold dilution of a saturated Vx-770 solution.
evidence: This is inferred from the dose-response data showing K0.5 values much lower than the saturation concentration.

claim: It might be worth testing whether drug doses lower than currently approved dosages are equally beneficial to CF patients.
source: Thus, it might be worth testing whether drug doses lower than the currently approved dosage regimes are equally beneficial to CF patients, as this could reduce treatment costs that are currently ~300000 USD/patient/year.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on the finding of high drug potency.

claim: Current treatment costs for Vx-770 are approximately $300,000 USD per patient per year.
source: as this could reduce treatment costs that are currently ~300000 USD/patient/year.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about current treatment costs.

claim: Vx-770 dissolved in 1-octanol shows strong absorption with a peak at 311 nm.
source: Vx-770 dissolved in 1-octanol at 1–4 μM showed clearly measurable light absorption with a peak at 311 nm (Figure 1b, blue spectra)
evidence: This is supported by spectrophotometric measurements shown in Figure 1b.

claim: The time constant for current decline following Vx-770 removal is approximately 2 minutes.
source: However, upon drug removal the current readily declined back to its pre-drug value (time constant τ ~2 min, Figure 2a, red fit line)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and exponential fitting shown in Figure 2a.

claim: A 20-fold dilution of the 1x saturated Vx-770 stock stimulates WT CFTR open probability by approximately 4-fold.
source: In single-channel recordings (Figure 2b), even a 20-fold dilution of our 1x saturated Vx-770 stock stimulated open probability of WT CFTR to a comparable level, by ~4 fold (Figure 2c, left).
evidence: This is supported by single-channel experimental data shown in Figure 2b and 2c.

claim: The open probability of prephosphorylated WT CFTR channels in ATP is approximately 0.16.
source: To calculate the value of Ct, the total number of channels in the patch (N) was estimated by assuming Po;bas=0.16 for prephosphorylated channels in ATP (cf., Figure 2c).
evidence: This is stated in the methods and supported by data in Figure 2c.

claim: The Hill coefficient for Vx-770 stimulation of WT CFTR is approximately 1.3.
source: Hill coefficients were 1.31±0.65 and 1.32±0.47 for WT in Vx-770 or Vx-770/DMSO
evidence: This is obtained from fitting dose-response curves shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The Hill coefficient for Vx-770 stimulation of ΔF508 CFTR is approximately 1.12.
source: Hill coefficients were 1.31±0.65 and 1.32±0.47 for WT in Vx-770 or Vx-770/DMSO, 1.12±0.07 for ΔF508
evidence: This is obtained from fitting dose-response curves shown in Figure 3f.

claim: The Hill coefficient for Vx-770 stimulation of G551D CFTR is approximately 1.22.
source: Hill coefficients were 1.31±0.65 and 1.32±0.47 for WT in Vx-770 or Vx-770/DMSO, 1.12±0.07 for ΔF508, and 1.22±0.10 for G551D CFTR.
evidence: This is obtained from fitting dose-response curves shown in Figure 3f.

claim: At subnanomolar/low nanomolar aqueous drug concentrations, current stimulation starts with a marked delay of up to approximately 1 minute.
source: In particular, at subnanomolar/low nanomolar aqueous drug concentrations current stimulation started off with a marked delay of up to ~1 min (Figure 4a, gray trace)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Slow drug accumulation in the membrane is required for CFTR potentiation by Vx-770.
source: In particular, at subnanomolar/low nanomolar aqueous drug concentrations current stimulation started off with a marked delay of up to ~1 min (Figure 4a, gray trace), consistent with slow drug accumulation in the membrane being required for CFTR potentiation (Jih and Hwang, 2013).
evidence: This is inferred from the delayed activation kinetics and supported by citation.

claim: The deactivation rate following Vx-770 removal is independent of drug concentration.
source: As expected, deactivation rate (1/τoff) was independent of drug concentration (Figure 4c)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: The overall rate of activation by Vx-770 becomes faster at higher drug concentrations.
source: whereas the overall rate of activation (1/τon*, see Materials and methods) became faster at higher concentrations (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: At the single-channel level, both application and removal of low concentrations of Vx-770 cause abrupt changes in channel open probability with marked delay.
source: At a single-channel level both application and removal of low concentrations of Vx-770 (Figure 4d, top, red bar) caused abrupt changes in channel open probability, but with a marked delay (Figure 4d, stability plot, red vs. gray bars; bottom, expanded current segments).
evidence: This is supported by single-channel experimental data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: A recent study suggested two potential binding sites for Vx-770 in the transmembrane domains of CFTR.
source: Of note, a recent study suggested two potential binding sites for Vx-770 in the transmembrane domains of CFTR (Yeh et al., 2019).
evidence: This is based on a citation to a recent study.

claim: Mutations introduced into either of two putative Vx-770 binding sites strongly impaired potentiation by both GLPG-1837 and Vx-770.
source: Interestingly, mutations introduced into either of two putative sites strongly impaired potentiation by both GLPG-1837 and Vx-770 (Yeh et al., 2019).
evidence: This is based on a citation to a recent study.

claim: Scheme 3 predicts an apparent Hill slope of approximately 1.17.
source: Of note, Scheme 3 predicts an apparent Hill slope of only ~1.17 (see Materials and methods) which is consistent with the values obtained both for GLPG-1837 by Yeh and colleagues, and for Vx-770 in the present study (Figure 3).
evidence: This is calculated from the kinetic model and compared with experimental data.

claim: Scheme 3 is the best current working model for describing the molecular mechanism of CFTR potentiation by Vx-770.
source: We therefore consider Scheme 3 the best current working model for describing the molecular mechanism of CFTR potentiation by Vx-770.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the quality of fits and consistency with experimental observations.

claim: The entropy increase associated with the Vx-770 solution process is +10.1 kJ/mol at 25°C.
source: Thus, the thermodynamic explanation for the extremely low aqueous solubility of Vx-770 is that the entropy increase (TΔSosol = +10.1 kJ/mol at 25°C) associated with the solution process is too small to compensate for the large increase in enthalpy, likely caused by the disruption of hydrogen bonds between water molecules.
evidence: This is calculated from the measured thermodynamic parameters.

claim: The extremely low aqueous solubility of Vx-770 is due to the entropy increase being too small to compensate for the large increase in enthalpy.
source: Thus, the thermodynamic explanation for the extremely low aqueous solubility of Vx-770 is that the entropy increase (TΔSosol = +10.1 kJ/mol at 25°C) associated with the solution process is too small to compensate for the large increase in enthalpy, likely caused by the disruption of hydrogen bonds between water molecules.
evidence: This is inferred from the calculated thermodynamic parameters.

claim: The large increase in enthalpy during Vx-770 solution is likely caused by disruption of hydrogen bonds between water molecules.
source: Thus, the thermodynamic explanation for the extremely low aqueous solubility of Vx-770 is that the entropy increase (TΔSosol = +10.1 kJ/mol at 25°C) associated with the solution process is too small to compensate for the large increase in enthalpy, likely caused by the disruption of hydrogen bonds between water molecules.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on thermodynamic data and chemical principles.

claim: Vx-770 was identified by Vertex Pharmaceuticals using high-throughput screening.
source: The potentiator Vx-770 (Van Goor et al., 2009), identified by Vertex Pharmaceuticals using high-throughput screening
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Treatment with Vx-770 is accepted as the standard of care for the majority of CF patients in the US.
source: Although treatment with Vx-770 (administered orally, either alone or in combination with corrector drugs) is accepted as the standard of care for the majority of CF patients in the US
evidence: This is established knowledge about current clinical practice.

claim: Vx-770 contains two potentially deprotonatable groups.
source: This transmembrane pH gradient might influence the distribution of Vx-770 in the body, as the drug contains two potentially deprotonatable groups (Figure 1a, red arrows)
evidence: This is based on the chemical structure shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The computationally predicted strongest acidic pKa value of Vx-770 varies between 6.57 and 8.66 depending on the method of prediction.
source: Because the computationally (Chemaxon) predicted strongest acidic pKa value varies between 6.57 and 8.66, depending on the method of prediction
evidence: This is based on computational predictions using Chemaxon software.

claim: The smallest acidic pKa value of Vx-770 is substantially higher than 7.4.
source: This finding suggests that the strongest acidic pKa value of the drug is substantially higher than 7.4
evidence: This is inferred from the pH-independence of solubility measurements.

claim: The aqueous solubility of Vx-770 is similar in the cytosol and extracellular space.
source: The corollary is that the aqueous solubility of the drug is similar in the cytosol and the extracellular space.
evidence: This is inferred from the finding that the drug remains uncharged across the physiological pH range.

claim: Vx-770 shows good oral bioavailability.
source: Vx-770 shows good oral bioavailability
evidence: This is established knowledge from pharmacokinetic studies.

claim: Plasma proteins increase drug transport capacity of blood and act as a drug buffer system.
source: In the plasma, most of the drug is bound to plasma proteins, which are important for its pharmacokinetics, as they tremendously increase the drug transport capacity of the blood and therefore oral bioavailability, and act as a drug buffer system that replenishes the free drug pool during the time course of its elimination from the body.
evidence: This is established pharmacokinetic knowledge.

claim: Target cell membranes will accumulate Vx-770 only to an extent that is at equilibrium with free dissolved Vx-770.
source: Therefore, in a living organism the target cell membranes will accumulate Vx-770 only to an extent that is at equilibrium with free dissolved Vx-770 (in the extracellular fluid and/or in the cytosol).
evidence: This is based on established principles of drug distribution.

claim: The measured aqueous solubility establishes an upper limit for free dissolved Vx-770 concentration that determines maximal drug concentration achievable in target cell membranes.
source: In the present study, we have established an upper limit for the latter parameter, which thus determines the maximal possible drug concentration achievable in target cell membranes.
evidence: This is inferred from the solubility measurements and principles of drug distribution.

claim: Vx-770 has five polar groups capable of hydrogen bonding.
source: One possible explanation for this slow apparent on-rate could be that the drug remains associated with the polar surface of the bilayer, consistent with the hydrogen bonding capability of its five polar groups (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is based on the chemical structure shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Diffusion coefficients of small molecules within a lipid bilayer fall in the range of 10^-8 to 10^-7 cm²/s.
source: Considering that measured diffusion coefficients of small molecules within a lipid bilayer fall in the range of 10−8 to 10−7 cm2/s (Ladha et al., 1996; Macháň and Hof, 2010)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: GLPG-1837 is a potentiator drug known to compete with Vx-770 for CFTR activation.
source: Recently, in silico docking to high-resolution CFTR structures of the potentiator GLPG-1837, a drug known to compete with Vx-770 for CFTR activation (Yeh et al., 2017), identified potential drug binding sites in CFTR's transmembrane domains (Yeh et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Dose response curves for GLPG-1837 activation are fitted with Hill coefficients close to unity.
